topics.description: An Iranian Kurdish woman whose death after detention by Iran's morality police in 2022 sparked nationwide protests.

parts.label: L
parts.question: This leader’s government urged nationals to leave Iran after a couple was accused of inciting protests for its secret service. For ten points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] Name this leader of En Marche, who was accused of hypocrisy by Iran for his management of the Yellow Vests protests. This president defeated Marine Le Pen to win re-election in 2022.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [H] Macron showed solidarity for protests over the September 2022 death of this woman. This woman fell into a coma after being detained by Iran’s “morality police.”
parts.answer: ANSWER: Mahsa Amini [accept either underlined portion]

parts.label: C
parts.question: [E] Mahsa Amini was arrested for improperly wearing one of these pieces of clothing, which are mandatory for Iranian women. Marine Le Pen advocated for a nationwide ban of these Islamic headscarves.

topics.description: A series of disputes and confrontations between Iceland and the United Kingdom over fishing rights in the North Atlantic from the 1950s through the 1970s.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: This practice was controlled by wealthy Basque merchants at Grand Banks in Newfoundland. The Magna Carta outlawed the use of weirs in this practice in England. One war over this practice ended after the UNCLOS defined Exclusive Economic Zones as within a range of (*) 200 nautical miles. Iceland and England fought a series of late 20th century “wars” over this practice in the North Sea. For 10 points, name this practice, which often yields animals like cod.

topics.description: British field marshal who commanded the allied forces that defeated Napoleon at the Battle of Waterloo in 1815.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: This battle ended the losing ruler’s “Hundred Days” period. One side’s forces in this battle were saved by the arrival of a Prussian Army under Gebhard von Blucher. After this battle, the leader of the losing side was permanently exiled to the island of (*) St. Helena. For 10 points, the Duke of Wellington won what 1815 battle, the final defeat for Napoleon Bonaparte?

topics.description: A network of caravan routes crossing the Sahara that exchanged West African gold for North African salt and other goods and supported states such as Ghana, Mali, and Songhai.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: The Kingdom of Mapungubwe controlled the trade of ivory and this resource in southern Africa until it was overtaken by the Kingdom of Zimbabwe. The ancient Egyptian word for this resource, nbw (“na-baw”), may be the source of the name of Nubia, which contained much of it. Camel caravans brought a different resource from sites like Taghaza to trade for this resource in cities like (*) Djenne. The market for this resource in Cairo crashed when Mansa Musa brought copious amounts of it with him on his hajj. The Trans-Saharan trade route for salt and this resource was fought over by empires like Songhai, Ghana, and Mali. For 10 points, name this precious metal with a yellow color.

topics.description: A 656 CE battle near Basra in which forces supporting Ali ibn Abi Talib defeated an opposing army led by Aisha, Talha, and al-Zubayr.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: A species of this animal derives its name from Roman soldiers stationed by Trajan in Palmyra. Khabirs were responsible for the well-being of these animals on the “Forty Days Road.” During Timur’s sack of Delhi, these animals were covered in straw and lit on fire to spook Mahmud Khan’s elephants. The dogs of Haw’ab barking at one of these animals may have preceded a battle near Basra in which Ali’s troops circled (*) Aisha. Domesticated examples of these animals like the Dromedary and Bactrian species were valued on the Silk Road as “ships of the desert.” Caravans across the Sahara traveled on, for 10 points, what humped animals?
parts.answer: camels [accept Bactrian camels; accept Dromedary camels; accept the Battle of the Camel]

topics.description: A Bantu-speaking ethnolinguistic people of Zimbabwe and neighboring regions whose ancestors built Great Zimbabwe and established the Kingdom of Mutapa.

parts.label: L
parts.question: A “Great” city that shares its name with this country was home to the Eastern Enclosure, where six  soapstone sculptures were found. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this country, where long-time dictator Robert Mugabe died in 2019.

parts.label: B
parts.question: A short-lived republic that became Zimbabwe was named after this founder of De Beers Diamond  Company, who was prime minister of the Cape Colony in the 1890s.

parts.label: C
parts.question: The builders of Great Zimbabwe were ancestors of this present-day Bantu people, who formed the  Kingdom of Mutapa (moo-TAP-uh) under Nyatsimba (nee-AHT-sim-bah).

topics.description: The July–August 1945 Allied conference near Berlin that addressed the administration and postwar settlement of Germany.

parts.label: L
parts.question: This program was named for the Secretary of State who proposed it in a 1947 speech at Harvard. For  10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [10] Name this American aid program that paid to rebuilt countries including West Germany after World  War II.
parts.answer: Marshall Plan [or European Recovery Program; or ERP]

parts.label: B
parts.question: [10] Marshall Plan funds were implemented in West Germany by this Christian Democratic Chancellor,  whose 1949 to 1963 time in office oversaw an “economic miracle.”

parts.label: C
parts.question: [10] West Germany's coal and steel industries were severely restricted for five years after this 1945  Allied conference held outside Berlin, which decided how to administer Germany after World War II.

topics.description: A 21 November 1920 episode of the Irish War of Independence in which British forces fired on a Gaelic football crowd at Croke Park in Dublin.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: Members of one of this country's political parties run for British parliament but do not take their seats. That party, Sinn Féin (shin fayn), was founded to fight for this country's independence. In 1920, British forces shot into a crowd of spectators watching a (*) Gaelic football match in this country's capital. For 10 points, what European country bordering the UK adopted a green-white-orange tricolor flag?
parts.answer: Republic of Ireland [or Poblacht na hÉireann; prompt on Northern Ireland or Tuaisceart Éireann until “independence” is read and do not accept or prompt afterwards]

topics.description: The late-19th-century gold rush that brought prospectors to the Klondike region of Yukon and nearby Alaska.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: The narrator tries to obtain Captain Kidd's treasure in an Edgar Allan Poe short story whose name contains this color. In the 1890s, many people travelled to places like Dawson City, Yukon after this material was discovered in the (*) Klondike. Prospectors used a technique called "panning" to obtain, for 10 points, what precious metal, which first-place medals at the Olympics are made out of?

topics.description: The October 1922 Fascist mobilization that pressured King Victor Emmanuel III to appoint Benito Mussolini prime minister of Italy.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: This leader received a ceremonial “Sword of Islam” from the native population of the “fourth shore” of this leader’s country. This leader guaranteed a two-thirds majority in Parliament to the party that received the largest share of votes by passing the (*) Acerbo Law. This leader used claims of native irredentism to force King Zog into exile and justify his country’s occupation of Albania. Victor Emmanuel III appointed this leader as prime minister after this leader’s paramilitary army, the Blackshirts, marched on Rome. For 10 points, name this Fascist leader nicknamed “Il Duce” who led Italy during World War II.
